title: Count Subtrees with Digit Sum K
statement:
You are given a binary tree whose nodes hold non-negative integers, and an integer `K`. The **digit sum** of a value is the sum of its decimal digits (for example the digit sum of `4075` is `16`, and of `0` is `0`).

A **subtree** is a node together with all of its descendants. Count the subtrees in which **every node** (the subtree's root included) has a value whose digit sum is exactly `K`.

Every node is the root of exactly one subtree, so a leaf whose own digit sum is `K` counts as one subtree, and a node counts only if its own digit sum is `K` and both of its child subtrees (when present) also qualify.

Print the number of qualifying subtrees.

**Follow-up:** the original question was also reported as "count the subtrees in which all nodes share the same digit sum" (no `K` given). Can you count those in a single pass as well? This variant is not tested here.
inputFormat:
The first line contains the integer `K`.
The second line contains the tree in level order, separated by spaces, using `null` for a missing child. Children of a `null` entry are not listed, and trailing `null` entries may be omitted. The first entry is the root and is never `null`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the number of subtrees in which every node has digit sum `K`.
constraints: The height of the tree is at most 5000

examples.explanation: The tree has root 14 with children 5 and 32; node 5 has right child 41; node 32 has children 23 and 7. Digit sums: 14, 5, 32, 41 and 23 all have digit sum 5, but 7 does not. The leaves 41 and 23 qualify, and so does node 5 (its only descendant is 41). Node 7 fails, which also disqualifies 32 and the root. Total 3.
Root 10 has children 100 and 1; node 1 has children 10 and 5. Leaves 100 and 10 have digit sum 1 and count. Leaf 5 has digit sum 5, so node 1 and the root are disqualified. Total 2.
A single node of value 0 has digit sum 0, which equals K, so the one subtree counts.

hints: A subtree qualifies only if its root has digit sum K and every child subtree qualifies as well, so the answer for a node depends on the answers for its children.
Compute a boolean per node bottom-up (post-order): good(node) = digitsum(node) == K and good(left) and good(right), treating a missing child as good.
Count the nodes for which good is true. Each node is visited once and its digit sum costs at most 10 steps.
